Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the left hemithorax with contralateral (rightward) tracheal deviation, which indicates a space-occupying lesion such as a massive pleural effusion rather than lung collapse (which would cause ipsilateral deviation). Among the choices, a large pleural effusion causing rightward displacement is the only option consistent with this radiographic sign.
